definition: The time between two events measured in the inertial frame in which both happen at the same place, so one clock times them both; it is the shortest interval any inertial observer measures.
The length of an object measured in the inertial frame in which the object is at rest; it is the longest length any inertial observer measures.
The lengthening of the time between two events for an observer who sees them happen at different places, $\Delta t = \gamma\Delta t_0$, so a clock moving relative to you is measured to run slow.
The shortening of an object's length along its direction of motion for an observer who sees it move, $L = \frac{L_0}{\gamma}$; lengths at right angles to the motion do not change.
Two events happening at the same time in a given frame; events at different places that are simultaneous in one inertial frame need not be simultaneous in another.
